cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Every Glitch Is a Gift
cards.instruction: Turn every contradiction or failure into a surprising benefit of the impossible system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office clock has sent us backward. Excellent; we can prepare for the meeting we missed. Open your calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too far. The invitation hasn't arrived. I'll turn the clock forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave it. We have preparation time now. Draft the questions before you start accepting invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we're before the booking. The boss is asking whether the meeting's needed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. Send her the questions as an email. Please solve them before you suggest putting six people in a room.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects clock adjustment and work sequence, while A5 replaces a meeting proposal with solving questions, making expert planning exploit every backward overshoot.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 decision point to prevent the meeting rather than merely improve attendance.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 email instruction is practical; six people is an ordinary estimate but not needed to understand the improvement.
